name: Sri Lanka
official: Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

story: In 2022 Sri Lanka ran out of dollars to buy fuel, food and medicine, defaulted on its debts, and crowds stormed the presidential palace and swam in the president's pool. In 2024 voters swept away the dynasties that had run the country for decades and elected Anura Kumara Dissanayake, leader of a Marxist party that once led armed uprisings, who then won a two-thirds majority in parliament. By late 2025 his government had become an IMF success story. Then the weather struck.

Cyclone Ditwah hit on 26 November 2025 and its floods and landslides killed more than 640 people, affected 2.3 million, over a tenth of the population, and touched all 25 districts; the total damage is thought to exceed the 2004 tsunami's (AFP via eNCA). Dissanayake called it the most challenging natural disaster in the island's history. Officials estimated reconstruction at $6 to 7 billion. In 2026 the government is trying to rebuild without breaking the fragile recovery: it approved 500 billion rupees, about $1.6 billion, in extra spending without raising its borrowing limit, offered survivors up to 10 million rupees to resettle on safer land, and secured emergency IMF funding of $206 million. In January the IMF confirmed its bailout would continue unchanged, citing the government's "strong fiscal discipline" (Business Standard). Analysts warn the shock shows how exposed a debt-distressed country remains (East Asia Forum).
briefing.power: A semi-presidential republic. The directly elected president, limited to two five-year terms, heads state and government and appoints the prime minister and cabinet; the 225-seat parliament is elected by proportional representation.
briefing.holders: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake (National People's Power), since 2024; Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya.
